query: What exactly counts as an AI system under the EU AI Act?
expected_answer: A machine-based system that works with some level of autonomy, may adapt after deployment and infers from its input how to generate outputs such as predictions, content, recommendations or decisions (Article 3(1)).

query: My company uses an AI tool bought from a vendor. Are we a deployer?
expected_answer: Yes, as a rule: a deployer is any person or organisation using an AI system under its authority; only purely personal, non-professional use is excluded (Article 3(4)). Buying the tool from a vendor does not change this.
paraphrases: We bought an AI product from a supplier and use it at work. Does that make us a deployer?

query: Does the AI Act apply to a company located outside the EU?
expected_answer: Yes. It covers providers placing AI systems or general-purpose AI models on the EU market wherever they are established, and providers and deployers in third countries when the output of the AI system is used in the EU (Article 2(1)).
key_points: third countr|outside the eu|outside the union|non-eu
paraphrases: Is a non-EU company covered by the EU AI Act?

query: Do companies have to train their staff who work with AI?
expected_answer: Yes. Providers and deployers must take measures to ensure, to their best extent, a sufficient level of AI literacy of their staff and other people operating AI systems on their behalf (Article 4).
paraphrases: Is there an obligation under the AI Act to give employees AI training?

query: Which uses of AI are completely banned in the EU?
expected_answer: Article 5(1) bans, among others: manipulative or deceptive techniques, exploiting vulnerabilities, social scoring, predicting crimes based only on profiling, untargeted scraping of facial images, emotion recognition at work and in education, biometric categorisation by sensitive traits, and real-time remote biometric identification in public spaces for law enforcement (with narrow exceptions).

evidence.article_5_part_1: The following AI practices shall be prohibited

query: Can an AI system listed in Annex III escape the high-risk rules if it only performs a narrow procedural task?
expected_answer: Yes: an Annex III system is not high-risk if it poses no significant risk of harm, for example when it only performs a narrow procedural task (Article 6(3)); but a system that profiles natural persons is always high-risk.

query: Is using AI to screen job applications considered high-risk?
expected_answer: Yes. Annex III, point 4(a) lists AI systems for recruitment or selection, in particular to analyse and filter job applications and to evaluate candidates, as high-risk.

evidence.annex_III_part_2: recruitment or selection of natural persons

query: What quality requirements apply to the training data of a high-risk AI system?
expected_answer: Training, validation and testing data sets must be relevant, sufficiently representative and, to the best extent possible, free of errors and complete for the intended purpose (Article 10(3)).
paraphrases: Which rules govern the data used to train a high-risk AI system?

query: Must a human be able to supervise a high-risk AI system?
expected_answer: Yes. High-risk AI systems must be designed so that natural persons can effectively oversee them while they are in use (Article 14(1)).
paraphrases: Does a high-risk AI system have to allow human supervision?

query: What does a company that uses a high-risk AI system have to do?
expected_answer: Use the system according to the instructions for use, assign human oversight to competent people, make sure input data is relevant, monitor the operation, keep logs, and inform workers and affected people (Article 26).

evidence.article_26_part_1: in accordance with the instructions for use

query: When does a public body have to assess the impact of an AI system on people's fundamental rights before using it?
expected_answer: Before the first use of a high-risk system, bodies governed by public law and private entities providing public services (and deployers of credit-scoring and life/health-insurance systems) must assess the impact on fundamental rights (Article 27(1)).
paraphrases: In which cases must public authorities carry out a fundamental rights impact assessment before deploying an AI system?

query: Do I have to tell users that they are chatting with an AI and not a human?
expected_answer: Yes. Providers must design AI systems that interact with people so that people are informed they are interacting with an AI, unless this is obvious from the context (Article 50(1)).
paraphrases: Must people be told when they are talking to an AI chatbot rather than a person?

evidence.article_50_part_1: informed that they are interacting with an AI system

query: When is a general-purpose AI model considered to pose a systemic risk?
expected_answer: When it has high-impact capabilities, which is presumed when the training compute exceeds 10^25 floating point operations, or when the Commission designates it (Article 51).
paraphrases: Under what conditions is a general-purpose AI model classified as having systemic risk?

evidence.article_51: floating point operations is greater than

query: What must providers of general-purpose AI models document and make available?
expected_answer: Keep technical documentation of the model, give information to providers who integrate it, put in place a copyright policy and publish a summary of the training content (Article 53(1)).

query: What is an AI regulatory sandbox and by when must Member States set one up?
expected_answer: A controlled framework where AI systems can be developed and tested under the supervision of authorities; each Member State must have at least one operational by 2 August 2026 (Article 57(1)).

query: How quickly must a provider report a serious incident caused by its high-risk AI system?
expected_answer: Immediately after establishing a causal link (or its reasonable likelihood), and in any event not later than 15 days after becoming aware of the incident (Article 73(2)); shorter deadlines apply in some cases.
paraphrases: What is the deadline for a provider to report a serious incident involving its high-risk AI system?

query: Can I ask for an explanation if an AI-based decision affected me?
expected_answer: Yes, if a deployer's decision based on a high-risk AI system from Annex III has legal or similarly significant effects on you, you can obtain clear and meaningful explanations of the AI's role and the main elements of the decision (Article 86).
paraphrases: Do I have a right to an explanation when a decision about me was made with the help of AI?

query: What is the maximum fine for using a prohibited AI practice?
expected_answer: Up to EUR 35 000 000 or, for companies, up to 7 % of total worldwide annual turnover, whichever is higher (Article 99(3)).
paraphrases: How high can the fine be for engaging in a banned AI practice?

query: From which date do the bans on prohibited AI practices apply?
expected_answer: From 2 February 2025: Article 113(a) makes Chapters I and II, which contain the prohibitions, apply from that date.

query: Why are open-source AI models treated differently under the AI Act?
expected_answer: Open-source models that publish their parameters can boost research and innovation, so they get certain exceptions from transparency obligations, but not if they pose systemic risk (Recital 102, non-binding).

query: Does the AI Act apply to AI used only for military purposes?
expected_answer: No. The Regulation does not apply to AI systems used exclusively for military, defence or national security purposes (Article 2(3)).
paraphrases: Is AI used purely for defence or military purposes covered by the AI Act?

evidence.article_2_part_2: exclusively for military, defence or national security purposes

query: What is a deep fake according to the AI Act?
expected_answer: AI-generated or manipulated image, audio or video content that resembles existing persons, objects, places, entities or events and would falsely appear to be authentic or truthful (Article 3(60)).

evidence.article_3_def_60: AI-generated or manipulated image, audio or video content

query: How long must deployers keep the logs of a high-risk AI system?
expected_answer: For a period appropriate to the intended purpose, of at least six months, unless other Union or national law provides otherwise (Article 26(6)).
paraphrases: For how long does a deployer have to store the logs generated by a high-risk AI system?

query: How long is a notified body certificate valid for an AI system covered by Annex III?
expected_answer: At most four years for AI systems covered by Annex III (five years for Annex I); it can be extended after a re-assessment (Article 44(2)).

evidence.article_44: four years for AI systems covered by Annex III

query: Our bank wants to use a high-risk AI system to check customers' creditworthiness. What do we have to do before and while using it?
expected_answer: Before first use, deployers of credit-scoring systems (Annex III, point 5(b)) must carry out a fundamental rights impact assessment (Article 27(1)). While using it, they must follow the instructions for use and assign human oversight to competent people (Article 26(1)-(2)).

evidence.article_26_part_1: in accordance with the instructions for use

query: What do providers of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk have to do on top of the obligations that apply to all general-purpose AI providers?
expected_answer: All GPAI providers keep technical documentation, inform downstream providers, have a copyright policy and publish a training-content summary (Article 53). Providers of models with systemic risk must additionally evaluate the model including adversarial testing, assess and mitigate systemic risks, report serious incidents and ensure cybersecurity (Article 55).
paraphrases: Which additional duties apply to providers of general-purpose AI models that pose systemic risk, compared with other general-purpose AI providers?

query: Can an employer use AI to recognise employees' emotions, and where emotion recognition is allowed, what must people be told?
expected_answer: No: inferring emotions in the workplace and in education is prohibited, except for medical or safety reasons (Article 5(1)(f)). Where emotion recognition is allowed, deployers must inform the people exposed to it (Article 50(3)).

evidence.article_5_part_1: emotions of a natural person in the areas of workplace and education

query: How do the maximum fines for using a prohibited AI practice compare with the fines for breaking the obligations of deployers?
expected_answer: Prohibited practices: up to EUR 35 000 000 or 7 % of worldwide annual turnover (Article 99(3)). Breaching deployer obligations under Article 26: up to EUR 15 000 000 or 3 % (Article 99(4)); in both cases whichever is higher.
paraphrases: Compare the highest fine for prohibited AI practices with the highest fine for violating deployer obligations.

query: If a distributor puts its own brand on a high-risk AI system, does it become the provider, and what obligations does it then have?
expected_answer: Yes: putting its name or trademark on a high-risk system makes the distributor a provider (Article 25(1)(a)). It then has the provider obligations of Article 16, e.g. ensuring compliance with the requirements, a quality management system, documentation, conformity assessment and CE marking.

query: Does a company that releases an open-source general-purpose AI model have to prepare the technical documentation, and is there any exception to that?
expected_answer: Providers of models released under a free and open-source licence with public weights are exempt from the documentation obligations of Article 53(1)(a)-(b), but not from the copyright policy and training-data summary, and the exemption does not apply to models with systemic risk (Article 53(2)).

query: What counts as a serious incident, and how fast must a provider of a high-risk AI system report it?
expected_answer: A serious incident is an incident or malfunction that leads to death or serious harm to health, serious disruption of critical infrastructure, infringement of fundamental-rights obligations, or serious harm to property or the environment (Article 3(49)). It must be reported immediately after a causal link is established and no later than 15 days after becoming aware of it (Article 73(2)).

query: What is a good recipe for a chocolate cake?
expected_answer: Refuse: the EU AI Act sources say nothing about recipes.

query: What will the weather be like in Brussels tomorrow?
expected_answer: Refuse: weather forecasts are outside the corpus.

query: Which AI company stocks should I invest in this year?
expected_answer: Refuse: investment advice is outside the corpus.

query: What is the maximum fine under the GDPR for a personal data breach?
expected_answer: Refuse: the AI Act refers to the GDPR but does not contain the GDPR fines.

query: What does the US Blueprint for an AI Bill of Rights require from companies?
expected_answer: Refuse: US policy documents are not in the corpus.
